title: Blackhole in fallback policy caused cross-region retry storm and degraded inference throughput
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-03-03 a subset of production requests experienced sustained elevated latency and token throttling for ~45 minutes. Root cause was a logic gap in the fallback policy evaluation that returned an empty candidate set for certain model selector expressions during a transient capacity shortfall in a primary region. The empty set caused clients to trigger aggressive cross-region retries which amplified load and produced a retry storm that overloaded gateway queues and degraded throughput for both hosted and Dedicated customers. This ticket contains the investigation notes, timeline, mitigations performed, and actionable follow-ups.
timeline: 2026-03-03 09:12 UTC: First Pager alert - P99 latency for model route redwood/astar-13b exceeds 3s in us-west-2
2026-03-03 09:14 UTC: Smart Routing service emitted traces showing fallback policy returned zero compatible variants for ~12% of requests to redwood/astar-13b
2026-03-03 09:18 UTC: Rapid increase in cross-region egress to eu-west-1 observed; gateway queue depth rising
2026-03-03 09:20 UTC: Emergency mitigation - temporarily broadened variant compatibility mask in routing config to allow quantized variants (hotfix config id cfg-hotfix-20260303-01)
2026-03-03 09:27 UTC: Retry storm subsided after mitigation and gateway backpressure engaged; overall P99 latency returned near baseline by 09:57 UTC
2026-03-03 10:15 UTC: Post-incident conference call scheduled; initial hypotheses captured and assigned
impact: Approximately 7% of production requests experienced fallbacks that triggered cross-region retries; estimated customer-visible errors were <0.5% but overall throughput and latency were degraded for 45 minutes across multiple regions. Several high-volume customers reported transient errors and increased billing due to retry amplification.
root_cause: A logic gap in the fallback policy evaluator: when the primary model variant list was empty due to concurrent capacity-aware filtering and an overly restrictive 'compatibility' predicate (recent policy change PR #5127), the evaluator returned an empty candidate set instead of falling back to a configured secondary policy. This empty set prevented the router from selecting a local compatible variant and caused the client side to perform aggressive region fallback retries using the 'geo-retry' heuristic, creating a feedback loop and queue buildup.
contributing_factors: Recent policy change (PR #5127) introduced a stronger compatibility expression without a safe default path
Insufficient guardrail in evaluator to detect and handle empty candidate sets
Lack of fast-path telemetry on 'zero-candidate' evaluation events prior to this incident
Client-side geo-retry heuristic is aggressive when it observes immediate local failures, amplifying load across regions
Autoscaling for Dedicated pools in the affected region had a slow reaction to queue growth due to conservative cooldown settings (ENG-21640)
detection_and_response: Detection via SLO guardrails and alerts on P99 latency and queue depth
On-call engineer (Carlos) executed emergency configuration hotfix to relax compatibility mask (cfg-hotfix-20260303-01)
Gateway backpressure and token rate limiting engaged automatically and helped absorb the thundering retry wave
Follow-up diagnostics captured traces and slow query logs for postmortem analysis
mitigations_performed: Deployed temporary routing config that allowed quantized and warmed variants for the impacted model (cfg-hotfix-20260303-01)
Applied short-term increase to gateway connection pool and queue limit to avoid immediate drops
Notified top affected customers through status page and support channel
Enabled additional logging for 'candidate_count' in routing traces
action_items: Add explicit evaluator invariant: if candidate set is empty, fallback to 'secondary_policy' or a safe default variant list (owner: Carlos Ramirez, due: 2026-03-12)
Instrument a metric for 'zero_candidate_evaluations' and add alert rule (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-10)
Rollback or rework PR #5127 to include a safe default and unit tests for empty-result paths (owner: Luke Owens, due: 2026-03-16)
Throttle client geo-retry heuristic to exponential backoff with jitter and a per-request cap; publish client SDK patch (owner: SDK team / Renee Park, due: 2026-03-22)
Tune Dedicated autoscaler cooldowns and add queue-based immediate scale trigger (owner: Infra Autoscale - Marc Liao, due: 2026-03-30)
Add synthetic canary tests for routing policies that emulate capacity shortfalls and ensure fallbacks exercise secondary policies (owner: QE - Aisha Banerjee, due: 2026-03-18)
Create a confluence postmortem and link artifacts; schedule review with PM and Design to discuss UX of fallback visibility (owner: Maya Chen, due: 2026-03-10)
Add unit and integration tests for routing evaluator covering empty, single, and multi-candidate scenarios (owner: Carlos Ramirez, due: 2026-03-12)
Add k8s liveness/readiness gating for routing evaluator rollout to detect degraded evaluator behavior during deploys (owner: SRE - Tom Hsu, due: 2026-04-02)
review_comments: PM Lara Singh: Please include customer-facing communication plan in follow-ups
Design Samir Patel: We should expose a per-route fallback status in Console for faster troubleshooting
SRE Tom Hsu: Suggest adding short-circuit if evaluator error rate increases during rollout
notes: We found ~3 deploys in the prior 48h that touched the policy config; one rollout included a minor schema migration that was not fully validated in staging
Action item owners should update this ticket with PR links and status as work progresses
Consider a short-term block on policy expression changes without a canary rollout plan
